content:
Apple has outlined plans to allow users to copy and paste content between iPhone and Windows PCs, in response to Microsoft's interoperability request in the European Union. Details below.

The feature may only be available in the EU region.

According to MacRumors, a new entry has appeared on Apple's EU interoperability request page, showing that the company has agreed to develop a solution that allows extensions to share and import iPhone clipboard items with paired devices (including Windows PCs).

In the original request Microsoft received on March 25, 2026, the company stated that it is currently unable to offer a feature comparable to Universal Clipboard, which allows users to copy and paste content between Apple devices.

Microsoft further asked Apple to provide persistent clipboard access for continuous syncing between iPhone and Windows PCs, and outlined three main use cases:

Copy text or other supported content on iPhone and paste directly into a Windows PC, and vice versa. For common productivity workflows, this should work without needing to switch apps to the foreground or repeatedly take explicit actions to initiate the transfer. Clipboard syncing should be a lightweight, continuous feature rather than a manual, app-driven operation.

The company argued that cross-device copy and paste is a basic productivity interaction that users expect to "just work" between their primary devices, and added that its intent is "not to replace or replicate Apple's system experience, but to deliver the basic level of cross-device productivity users already expect when working across their devices."

Apple subsequently replied on April 27, saying that after an initial assessment of Microsoft's request, it had decided to "move it to the next stage of our interoperability process."

Later, on June 26, Apple confirmed it would develop the relevant solution and outlined how it expects the feature to work.

The company also explained that Microsoft will need to rely on the AccessorySetupKit framework. This framework previously drew controversy in a similar interoperability request from Meta in the EU regarding AirPods pairing support, involving pairing across users' iPhone and iPad devices.

In Microsoft's case, AccessorySetupKit will be used to obtain permission to share clipboard content with a paired Windows PC, with users required to grant authorization once per device.

Apple described the project as a "significant engineering effort", saying it plans to complete development by fall 2027, with the solution to first appear in a developer beta before a full public release.

This timeline suggests the feature could launch as part of iOS 28, although Apple has not yet confirmed which software version it will be included in.
